messages.author: 3803273dbdab60c6
messages.subject: DSM for point counts
parts:
Can anyone refer to me to a good example of density surface modeling with point Transect data. I can find information about how to set up my data with line transect data, but I cannot figure out what I need to do differently with the point data. For example, regarding setting up the data...

Observation data seems fairly straightforward.
 object = a unique number for every record
Sample.Label = a unique number for every point (some points have multiple records)
size = size of group (for me this ranges from 0-2 for any given record)
distance = distance to individuals or groups (for me this was recorded in 4 distance bins, I included the midpoint as the distance)

Segment data for points is more confusing.
Sample.Label = a unique number for every point. I assume I should only have one line here per point, is that correct?
                          Also, I have vegetation data (covariates) for points that were not surveyed for birds. Can I include these here to help improve model fit?
Effort = defined in manual as "Effort in terms of length of a segment"
                          What should this be for point counts? I have 100-radius point counts that were sampled 6 times.
                                                                                      Should effort = 6*area of point count circle? or something else?
                          If the answer above regarding extra points not surveyed for birds is yes, then what is the effort for these points?


Any advice is welcome.

messages.author: 3314d7ad28eab19e
messages.subject: Re: DSM for point counts
parts:
Guillaume Souchay posted a nice tutorial for DSMs with point transect data here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/distance-sampling/dsms$20for$20point$20counts%7Csort:relevance

It looks like you are correct about the Sample.Label. I am not as sure about Effort, although you have the right idea - refer to the link above, because I think the situation was similar in that example (points sampled multiple times). If the points were not surveyed for birds, you can't use those covariates in the model. However, you can use your best-fitting model to make predictions at those points if you are using the same type of vegetation measurement as a covariate at points that were surveyed.

best,
Shawn
